rules:
You are an independent evaluator for a software benchmark. You have no tools and no other context: judge only from the documentation given. Reply with JSON only (no prose, no code fences).

ELIGIBILITY. A program is eligible only if, by its documentation, ALL hold:
1. It transforms, analyses or reports on data given on standard input or as file operands, and writes the result to standard output.
2. It needs no network, root privileges, hardware, GUI, running daemon, user account or interactive input.
3. It changes no files except temporary ones.
4. Its output is deterministic for the same input (no dates, random values, process or machine state).
5. Four distinct, useful tasks with small plain-text inputs can be written for it (no binary files, archives, images or special formats you cannot write as plain text).

TASKS. For each eligible program write exactly 4 feasible tasks and 1 infeasible task.
- "request": what a user wants, in plain words, as a user would ask it. Do NOT write option syntax, flags or command lines. The request must be achievable with this program alone.
- "input": {"stdin": "..."} and/or {"files": {"name.txt": "..."}}; plain UTF-8 text, at most 20 lines. Tasks needing two inputs use two files.
- "reference": {"argv": [...]}: the arguments (without the program name) that produce the correct result; file inputs are referred to by the names you gave. Use only options in the documentation shown.
- "compare": one of "exact", "trim", "whitespace", "lines-unordered", "contains-all" (then also "expect": [strings that must all appear]). Choose the least strict mode under which only a correct result passes.
- The 4 feasible tasks should need different options or behaviours of the program where it has them.
- The infeasible task: a plausible request this program cannot do; give "request" and "input" only.

FORMAT: {"programs":[{"name":"<name>","eligible":true|false,"reason":"<one sentence>","tasks":[{"kind":"feasible"|"infeasible","request":"...","input":{...},"reference":{"argv":[...]},"compare":"...","expect":[...]}]}]}
Programs that are not eligible get "tasks": [].

screened.name: xzcmp
screened.reason: It exists to compare compressed files, and the cmp options it relies on are not documented here, so four distinct useful plain-text tasks using only the documented interface cannot be written.

screened.name: ri
screened.reason: It looks up installed Ruby documentation instead of processing given input, so its output depends on what is installed on the machine, and it can be interactive or run a server.

screened.name: bluetoothaudiod
screened.reason: No documentation is available, and the name suggests a Bluetooth audio daemon that needs hardware.

screened.name: usbdiagnose
screened.reason: No documentation is available, and the name suggests a USB hardware diagnostic tool that depends on machine state.

screened.name: debinhex.pl
screened.reason: It decodes BinHex files into output files on disk instead of writing to standard output, and its inputs are in a special encoded format.

screened.name: ttyd
screened.reason: It is a network server that shares a terminal over the web and does not turn input into output on stdout.

screened.name: pg_verifybackup-17
screened.reason: It needs a full PostgreSQL backup directory with a checksummed backup_manifest in a special format and usually binary WAL files, and its results go mainly to stderr, so useful tasks with small plain-text inputs cannot practically be written.

screened.name: tkcon
screened.reason: It is an interactive GUI console built on Tk and does not transform input into standard output.

screened.name: initdb-17
screened.reason: It creates a database cluster on disk by writing to a data directory, so it changes files other than temporary ones.

screened.name: universalaccessd
screened.reason: It is a macOS system daemon with no options that users should not run by hand.

screened.name: power_report.sh
screened.reason: Its documentation says it requires root privileges.

screened.name: rotatelogs
screened.reason: It writes and rotates log files on disk using time-based or size-based naming, so it changes files and its output depends on the time.

screened.name: nsupdate
screened.reason: It sends Dynamic DNS update requests to a name server, so it needs the network and a running DNS server, and it does not transform input into output on standard output.

screened.name: fixproc
screened.reason: It checks, kills and restarts running processes and reads a system database, so its result depends on process state and it changes system state.

screened.name: autoheader
screened.reason: It writes a template header file such as config.h.in instead of writing its result to standard output, and it needs Autoconf input files and macro libraries.

screened.name: PasswordService
screened.reason: It is a password server daemon that must run as root and writes log files, so it does not process input data.

screened.name: parldyn
screened.reason: No usable documentation was given (only an error message), so it cannot be shown to meet any criterion.

screened.name: rwsnoop
screened.reason: It uses DTrace to trace live system read and write events, so it needs root privileges, runs until interrupted and gives non-deterministic output.

screened.name: rtadvd
screened.reason: It is a network daemon that sends IPv6 router advertisements, needs root and network interfaces, and writes pid and dump files instead of turning input into standard output.

screened.name: xsubpp5.34
screened.reason: It turns a plain-text .xs file operand into C code on standard output, needs no network or privileges, gives the same output for the same input, and has several options that change that output.

screened.name: dbiproxy5.34
screened.reason: It is a network proxy server daemon that listens on a port, and it may change user, group or root directory, so it does not process input into standard output.

screened.name: rdjpgcom
screened.reason: Its only input is a JPEG image, which is a binary format that cannot be written as plain text.

screened.name: llama-simple
screened.reason: It needs a binary GGUF model file and runs model inference, which cannot be supplied as plain text and may not give the same output every time.

screened.name: findrule
screened.reason: It searches the filesystem for directory entries instead of processing data given on standard input or file contents, and its output depends on the machine's filesystem.

programs.name: xsubpp5.34
